page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-48-lssd is an enterprise compute instance designed for heavy data architectures and high-density memory execution. It is powered by 48 dedicated virtual CPUs on an x86_64 processor architecture, paired with 378 GB of total system RAM. This provides approximately 7.88 GB of memory per core, creating a high-memory profile that accommodates large datasets directly in volatile memory without excessive swapping.

Storage is integrated directly on the host using four local NVMe solid-state drives totaling 1611 GB. By avoiding the protocol overhead and network hops associated with remote persistent disks, these bundled local drives deliver ultra-low access latencies and high throughput. This local storage configuration is well-suited for fast-access scratch disks, tempdb files, distributed file system caches, and real-time transaction logging where persistent network disk latency would introduce performance bottlenecks.

The instance excludes hardware accelerators such as GPUs, concentrating resource allocation entirely on general-purpose x86_64 compute and memory capacity. Qualitative cost efficiency is realized through the high density of memory and high-performance local NVMe storage within a single virtual machine boundary. Organizations can eliminate the need for multi-node clustering for workloads that fit comfortably within 378 GB of RAM and 1.6 TB of local disk, reducing management complexity and network overhead.

The physical configuration of c4d-highmem-48-lssd makes it tailored for memory-intensive and I/O-sensitive operational profiles. Core use cases include large in-memory databases, enterprise relational database management systems, high-volume caching platforms, real-time analytics engines, and data pipeline ETL staging where sustained compute and rapid disk throughput are critical.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-48-lssd is an x86_64 virtual instance configured for data-intensive enterprise tasks requiring high memory allocation alongside rapid local I/O performance. The server delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs matched with 378 GB of system memory, establishing a generous memory-to-core ratio of 7.88 GB per vCPU. Hardware integration includes 1611 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage distributed across four physical drives, allowing processes to bypass network storage latency for scratch space, transient indexing, or database journal operations. It operates without dedicated GPU acceleration, targeting computational and memory density rather than graphics or machine learning training. From an infrastructure cost perspective, bundling massive system RAM with integrated local NVMe capacity yields favorable operational efficiency for workloads that require high throughput without incurring network storage egress or provisioning overhead. This architecture provides a balanced profile for in-memory caches, distributed databases, large-scale extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, and enterprise analytics engines.
